original_value: With the revolution in smart infrastructure in the recent past, the smart healthcare system has been paid more considerable attention. The continuous upgradation of electricity meters to smart electricity devices has probed into a new market of intelligent data analysis services, providing aid to the health care systems. This paper presents a unified framework for extracting user behaviour patterns from home-based smart electricity meter data. The structure allows exploration and integration of frequent pattern growth algorithm for pattern mining and application of a variety of machine learning algorithms for categorizing the activities into manually labelled classes along with the implementation of Local Outlier Factor method for detection of an abnormal pattern of the inhabitant of smart homes. To evaluate the proposed framework, the work is implemented on the smart electricity dataset from the United Kingdom by separating the data into four distinct data files meant for the morning, afternoon, evening, and night energy utilization records. The results show a remarkable performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers with kappa statics greater than 0.95 for all time slots data. The resultant frequent device utilization patterns with anomaly score more than the threshold value, reflecting abnormal activity patterns, are found more in evening time data in comparison to other time slots, requiring the immediate attention of concerned healthcare authorities.

result.paraphrase: In the wake of recent advances in smart infrastructure, smart healthcare systems have drawn much greater attention. Ongoing upgrades of electricity meters into smart electrical devices have opened a new market for intelligent data analytics services that can support healthcare systems. This paper proposes a unified framework for mining user behavior patterns from home smart electricity meter data. The framework supports integrating the frequent pattern growth algorithm for pattern mining, applying multiple machine learning algorithms to classify activities into manually labeled classes, and using the Local Outlier Factor method to detect abnormal patterns in smart-home residents. To assess the proposed approach, it is implemented on a United Kingdom smart electricity dataset split into four separate files for morning, afternoon, evening, and night energy-use records. The results demonstrate strong performance from the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers, with kappa statistics above 0.95 across all time-slot data. The resulting frequent device-use patterns with anomaly scores above the threshold, indicating abnormal activity patterns, occur more often in the evening data than in the other time slots, calling for immediate attention from the relevant healthcare authorities.
